container_info.description: This project aims to develop a comprehensive functional test plan for Wi-Fi 7 (IEEE 802.11be) devices, focusing on non-performance aspects. The plan will cover Multi-Link Operation (MLO) with mandatory Multi-Link Single Radio (MLSR) and optional Multi-Link Multi Radio (MLMR) scenarios, security validation for WPA2 and WPA3 protocols, and basic stability test cases. The outcome will be a structured, reusable test plan suitable for device certification, QA, and interoperability testing.
container_info.reasoning: The project is focused on producing a structured, reusable test-plan and associated tooling for device certification/QA (server-side document generation, APIs, test orchestration) rather than a browser/mobile/desktop UI. The container is labeled backend and includes Python3, flask, uvicorn, celery and many backend tooling already preinstalled. Flask is lightweight, already present in the image, and appropriate for building simple REST APIs, documentation endpoints, and small orchestration services in a headless container with minimal dependencies. Uvicorn can be used for ASGI if needed and Celery (already present) can handle background test orchestration tasks.
requirements: virtualenv or venv for isolated environment (python -m venv .venv)
Werkzeug (installed as Flask dependency) - no extra production WSGI required
uvicorn if ASGI/async endpoints are desired (optional lightweight server)
basic requirements.txt with only essential packages: flask, requests (for test agents), pytest (lightweight test runner)
minimal configuration files: app entrypoint (app.py), simple Flask route(s) to serve API/docs, and simple CLI script to run headless server
lightweight storage: use file-based storage / SQLite (sqlite3) for any small persistence needs
optional: celery (already installed) and redis (already installed) only if background task queue is required; otherwise avoid
git (present) for source control; curl/wget for simple HTTP interactions
no production-grade webserver (nginx/gunicorn) or monitoring/logging stacks — use Flask dev server or uvicorn for containerized headless operation

steps.name: environment
steps.description: Verify required system commands (python3, pip3, sqlite3, ss/pgrep) exist and install only missing apt packages non-interactively. Create /etc/profile.d marker exporting CORE_DOC_GOV_WS (quoted) for workspace discovery. Create workspace folder and a small activate helper (activate.sh) that sources .venv when present. Operates in the authoritative workspace path. Avoid reinstalling tools that are already present in the container image; surface apt errors for diagnostics.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
# Only install missing packages; do not reinstall preinstalled tools from image
declare -A PKG_MAP=( [python3]=python3 [pip3]=python3-pip [sqlite3]=sqlite3 [lsof]=lsof )
missing_pkgs=()
command -v python3 >/dev/null || missing_pkgs+=("${PKG_MAP[python3]}")
command -v pip3 >/dev/null || missing_pkgs+=("${PKG_MAP[pip3]}")
command -v sqlite3 >/dev/null || missing_pkgs+=("${PKG_MAP[sqlite3]}")
# Check for socket/process utils; prefer ss/pgrep (usually present)
if ! command -v ss >/dev/null && ! command -v pgrep >/dev/null && ! command -v lsof >/dev/null; then
  missing_pkgs+=("${PKG_MAP[lsof]}")
fi
if [ ${#missing_pkgs[@]} -ne 0 ]; then
  sudo apt-get update -q || { echo "apt-get update failed" >&2; exit 2; }
  sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends "${missing_pkgs[@]}" || { echo "apt-get install failed for: ${missing_pkgs[*]}" >&2; exit 3; }
fi
# Write profile marker with quoted workspace to avoid shell parsing issues
PROFILE="/etc/profile.d/core_doc_gov_ws.sh"
if [ ! -f "$PROFILE" ]; then
  sudo bash -c "cat > '$PROFILE' <<'EOF'
# CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub workspace marker
export CORE_DOC_GOV_WS=\"$WORKSPACE\"
EOF"
fi
# Ensure workspace exists and provide local helper for venv activation
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE" && cd "$WORKSPACE"
cat > "$WORKSPACE/activate.sh" <<'EOF'
# source this file to activate the workspace venv: source ./activate.sh
if [ -f "$(pwd)/.venv/bin/activate" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  source "$(pwd)/.venv/bin/activate"
fi
EOF
chmod +x "$WORKSPACE/activate.sh"
# Validate basic tools are on PATH
python3 --version >/dev/null
pip3 --version >/dev/null
sqlite3 --version >/dev/null

set -euo pipefail

# Authoritative workspace from container info
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"

# Map commands to apt packages (only for those we may need to install)

command -v pip3 >/dev/null || missing_pkgs+=("${PKG_MAP[pip3]}")
command -v sqlite3 >/dev/null || missing_pkgs+=("${PKG_MAP[sqlite3]}")

export CORE_DOC_GOV_WS=\"$WORKSPACE\"
EOF"
fi

# Ensure workspace exists and create activate helper that sources .venv when present
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE" && cd "$WORKSPACE"
cat > "$WORKSPACE/activate.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# source this file to activate the workspace venv: source ./activate.sh
if [ -f "$(pwd)/.venv/bin/activate" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  source "$(pwd)/.venv/bin/activate"
fi
EOF

command -v sqlite3 >/dev/null || { echo "ERROR: sqlite3 not found on PATH after install" >&2; exit 6; }

# Print a short success summary (minimal output)
echo "environment: ok"

steps.name: scaffolding
steps.description: Create project structure, initialize a Python virtualenv (.venv) if missing, write pinned requirements.txt, scaffold app.py (minimal Flask with SQLite health route), and generate start scripts: start.sh (foreground using venv python) and run-bg.sh (background starter that captures PID immediately, writes PID atomically, uses DEV_SERVER_TIMEOUT for readiness, and validates PID ownership). Also add README and .gitignore. Operates inside the authoritative workspace path.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE" && cd "$WORKSPACE"
# Create venv if missing
if [ ! -d ".venv" ]; then
  python3 -m venv .venv
fi
VENV_PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
# Pinned minimal requirements
cat > requirements.txt <<'EOF'
flask==2.3.2
requests==2.31.0
pytest==7.4.2
EOF
# app.py minimal sqlite-backed health route
cat > app.py <<'EOF'
from flask import Flask, jsonify
import sqlite3
import os

DB_PATH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'data.db')

def init_db():
    if not os.path.exists(DB_PATH):
        conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
        conn.execute('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS kv (k TEXT PRIMARY KEY, v TEXT)')
        conn.commit()
        conn.close()

app = Flask(__name__)
init_db()

@app.route('/')
def index():
    return jsonify({"message":"CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub running"})

@app.route('/health')
def health():
    return jsonify({"status":"ok"})

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=5000)
EOF
# start.sh - foreground using venv python to run app.py directly for deterministic behavior
cat > start.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
VENV_PY="$DIR/.venv/bin/python"
if [ -x "$VENV_PY" ]; then
  exec "$VENV_PY" "$DIR/app.py"
else
  exec python3 "$DIR/app.py"
fi
EOF
chmod +x start.sh
# run-bg.sh - start server in background, capture $! immediately, write pid atomically, validate ownership
cat > run-bg.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
LOG="$DIR/.devserver.log"
PIDFILE="$DIR/.devserver.pid"
PORT=5000
TIMEOUT=${DEV_SERVER_TIMEOUT:-30}
# Idempotent: if PID running and valid, exit 0
if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
  pid=$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    # verify it's a python process and likely our app
    if ps -p "$pid" -o comm= | grep -i -E 'python|python3' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      exit 0
    fi
  fi
  rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true
fi
: >"$LOG"
# Activate venv if present
if [ -f "$DIR/.venv/bin/activate" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  source "$DIR/.venv/bin/activate"
fi
# Start server detached and capture the direct background PID
if [ -x "$DIR/.venv/bin/python" ]; then
  "$DIR/.venv/bin/python" "$DIR/app.py" >>"$LOG" 2>&1 &
else
  python3 "$DIR/app.py" >>"$LOG" 2>&1 &
fi
bgpid=$!
# Validate bgpid is a python process
if ! ps -p "$bgpid" -o comm= | grep -i -E 'python|python3' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # secondary fallback: try socket-based detection within TIMEOUT
  pid=""
  end=$((SECONDS+TIMEOUT))
  while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do
    if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      pid=$(ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null | awk -v port=":$PORT" '$4 ~ port {gsub(/.*pid=/,"",$6); gsub(/,.*$/,"",$6); print $6}') || true
    fi
    if [ -z "$pid" ] && command -v pgrep >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      pid=$(pgrep -f "python .*app.py|flask" || true)
    fi
    if [ -n "$pid" ]; then break; fi
    sleep 1
  done
  if [ -z "$pid" ]; then
    echo "failed to detect server process; see $LOG" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  bgpid=$pid
fi
# Write PID atomically
tmp="$PIDFILE.tmp"
echo "$bgpid" >"$tmp" && mv -f "$tmp" "$PIDFILE"
# Wait until health endpoint is reachable (TIMEOUT)
end=$((SECONDS+TIMEOUT))
while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do
  if curl -sS --fail http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep 1
done
# If we reach here, server didn't become ready
echo "server failed to become ready; tailing log:" >&2
tail -n 200 "$LOG" || true
exit 3
EOF
chmod +x run-bg.sh
# README and .gitignore
cat > README.md <<'EOF'
CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub

Use ./start.sh for foreground dev server (interactive). Use ./run-bg.sh to start backgrounded server with logs in .devserver.log. Activate venv with: source .venv/bin/activate or use ./activate.sh.
EOF
cat > .gitignore <<'EOF'
data.db
.devserver.log
.devserver.pid
.venv/
EOF

steps.name: dependencies
steps.description: Install Python dependencies into the workspace virtualenv non-interactively using pinned requirements. Use the workspace venv python binary explicitly to upgrade pip and install packages to avoid touching system Python. Log pip output to install.log, retry once on transient failures, and validate installed packages; exit with numeric codes on failures and print diagnostics.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
VENV_PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
if [ ! -x "$VENV_PY" ]; then
  echo "venv python not present; create venv first" >&2
  exit 2
fi
LOG="$WORKSPACE/install.log"
# Use venv python explicitly
if ! "$VENV_PY" -m pip install --upgrade pip >"$LOG" 2>&1; then
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2
  echo "pip upgrade failed" >&2
  exit 3
fi
# Install requirements with a single retry
if ! "$VENV_PY" -m pip install -r requirements.txt >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then
  sleep 1
  if ! "$VENV_PY" -m pip install -r requirements.txt >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then
    tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2
    exit 4
  fi
fi
# Verify pip is the venv pip
"$VENV_PY" -m pip --version >/dev/null
# Validate packages are importable and show versions; exit non-zero on missing pkg
"$VENV_PY" - <<'PY'
import importlib, sys
missing = []
for pkg in ("flask","requests","pytest"):
    try:
        m = importlib.import_module(pkg)
        ver = getattr(m, '__version__', getattr(m, 'VERSION', 'unknown'))
        print(pkg, ver)
    except Exception as e:
        print('missing', pkg, e, file=sys.stderr)
        missing.append(pkg)
if missing:
    sys.exit(2)
print('deps_ok')
PY

steps.description: Perform full validation: ensure dependencies import, start background server via run-bg.sh, poll readiness up to DEV_SERVER_TIMEOUT (default 30s), fetch and print health response and a short tail of logs as evidence, then stop server gracefully (SIGTERM then SIGKILL if needed) and clean up the PID file. steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
# Use venv python explicitly
VENV_PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
if [ ! -x "$VENV_PY" ]; then
  echo "venv python missing; run scaffold step" >&2
  exit 2
fi
LOG="$WORKSPACE/.devserver.log"
PIDFILE="$WORKSPACE/.devserver.pid"
TIMEOUT=${DEV_SERVER_TIMEOUT:-30}
# Ensure dependencies are importable
"$VENV_PY" - <<'PY'
import importlib, sys
for pkg in ("flask","requests"):
    try:
        importlib.import_module(pkg)
    except Exception as e:
        print('missing '+pkg, e, file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
print('deps_ok')
PY
# Start background server idempotently
./run-bg.sh
# Poll readiness up to TIMEOUT seconds
ready=0
end=$((SECONDS+TIMEOUT))
while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do
  if curl -sS --fail http://127.0.0.1:5000/health >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ready=1; break
  fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ "$ready" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "server failed to become ready; tailing log:" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" || true
  exit 5
fi
# Evidence: show health endpoint and short tail of logs
RESP=$(curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:5000/health || true)
echo "health_response:${RESP}"
echo "--- server log tail ---"
tail -n 50 "$LOG" || true
# Stop server gracefully with escalation, verify PID corresponds to python before kill
if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
  pid=$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "${pid:-}" ]; then
    if ps -p "$pid" -o comm= | grep -i -E 'python|python3' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      # wait up to 5s
      for i in {1..10}; do
        if ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
          break
        fi
        sleep 0.5
      done
      if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      fi
    else
      echo "PID $pid is not a python process; skipping kill" >&2
    fi
  fi
  rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# validation: ensure deps import, start run-bg.sh, poll readiness, show evidence, stop gracefully
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
VENV_PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
LOG="$WORKSPACE/.devserver.log"
PIDFILE="$WORKSPACE/.devserver.pid"
TIMEOUT=${DEV_SERVER_TIMEOUT:-30}
# 1) venv python presence
if [ ! -x "$VENV_PY" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: venv python missing at $VENV_PY; run scaffold step" >&2
  exit 2
fi
# 2) ensure dependencies importable
"$VENV_PY" - <<'PY'
import importlib, sys
missing=[]
for pkg in ("flask","requests"):
    try:
        importlib.import_module(pkg)
    except Exception as e:
        missing.append((pkg,str(e)))
if missing:
    for p,e in missing:
        print(f"ERROR: missing {p}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)
print('deps_ok')
PY
# 3) start background server idempotently via run-bg.sh
if [ ! -x ./run-bg.sh ]; then
  echo "ERROR: run-bg.sh missing or not executable in workspace" >&2
  exit 3
fi
# run run-bg.sh and capture its exit for diagnostics
if ! ./run-bg.sh; then
  echo "ERROR: run-bg.sh failed" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" || true
  exit 4
fi
# 4) poll readiness
ready=0
end=$((SECONDS+TIMEOUT))
while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do
  if curl -sS --fail http://127.0.0.1:5000/health >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ready=1; break
  fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ "$ready" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "ERROR: server failed to become ready within ${TIMEOUT}s; tailing log:" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" || true
  # attempt to cleanup PID if present
  if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
    echo "PID file present at $PIDFILE; content:" >&2
    cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  exit 5
fi
# 5) evidence: fetch health response and show log tail
RESP=$(curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:5000/health || true)
echo "health_response:${RESP}"
echo "--- server log tail ---"
tail -n 50 "$LOG" || true
# 6) graceful shutdown with verification of PID ownership
if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
  pid=$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "${pid:-}" ]; then
    if ps -p "$pid" -o comm= | grep -i -E 'python|python3' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      # wait up to ~5s for exit (10 * 0.5s)
      for i in {1..10}; do
        if ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
          break
        fi
        sleep 0.5
      done
      if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      fi
    else
      echo "WARNING: PID $pid is not a python process; skipping kill" >&2
    fi
  else
    echo "WARNING: PID file exists but is empty" >&2
  fi
  rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true
else
  echo "WARNING: PID file not found; server may have exited already" >&2
fi
# final: ensure server not running on port 5000
if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if ss -ltnp | grep -E ':5000\s' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "WARNING: something still listening on port 5000" >&2
    ss -ltnp | grep -E ':5000\s' || true
  fi
fi
echo "validation: SUCCESS"
